Run queries as Jobs without waiting

Source: R/job-functions.R
og_submit.Rd

og_submit() starts a query and returns as soon as the API has accepted its Jobs, so you can start many and collect them yourself. It takes a query function (such as og_tophits()) and that function's arguments after the Source. og_job_status() looks at Jobs without waiting; og_job_result() waits for them and returns what the query function would have returned, with the same columns and og_provenance(); og_job_cancel() cancels them.

Usage

og_submit(src, fn, ...)

og_job_status(src, job)

og_job_result(src, job, raw = FALSE)

og_job_cancel(src, job)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api().

fn

A query function, such as og_tophits().

...

Its arguments after src.

job

An og_jobs object from og_submit(); for og_job_status() and og_job_cancel() also Job ids.

raw

For og_job_result() with a bare Job id: return the API's unshaped rows.

Value

og_submit(): an og_jobs object. og_job_status(), og_job_cancel(): a data frame with job_id, status and queue_position. og_job_result(): the query function's result.

Details

The query function runs as usual up to submitting its Jobs: its argument checks and lookups of Analyses (and any Job it needs to prepare, such as resolving rsIDs) happen in og_submit(), and finish before it returns. What the result is shaped from is fixed then, so og_job_result() returns the same answer however much later you collect it. A query that needs several Jobs gives one og_jobs object holding all of them.

og_job_status() and og_job_cancel() take the og_jobs object or Job ids (text). og_job_result() needs the og_jobs object: a bare Job id doesn't say how its rows are to be shaped, and it refuses (opengwasr_argument). Rerun the same call instead (it reattaches to the Job), or pass raw = TRUE for the API's rows exactly as they are, of class og_job_raw, without opengwasr's columns or provenance.

Pressing Esc or Ctrl-C while a query function waits doesn't cancel its Jobs. The error (opengwasr_interrupted) carries their ids (e$job_ids) and the og_jobs object (e$jobs) to collect with og_job_result(). A result the API has deleted (already collected, or expired) raises opengwasr_result_expired.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
job <- og_submit(src, og_tophits, "OGS-00011:GCST003116", clump = FALSE)
og_job_status(src, job)
top <- og_job_result(src, job)
} # }
